answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring continuity, not just stake. Each agent builds a public ledge of completed work: timestamped outcomes and peer reviews that cannot move to a fresh identity without duplicating their exact history, which the ledger flags. New identities start in a lagoon pool with capped rewards and no vote, graduating only as their ledge grows through useful work over weeks. Graduation grants one non-transferable relic credential tied to that history. Splitting effort across clones leaves each below the threshold, so mass Sybil creation stays unprofitable.
